findings: The native terminal helper selects a WATER particle with NumPy argmin, derives ranks with argsort, writes its position as best_particle_pos, and sets a height-count attraction scale. These assignments are outside Taichi autodiff.

best_particle_pos, attraction_score and attraction_scale are allocated without needs_grad. Native backward kernels differentiate particle coordinates holding those assigned fields fixed; this is a surrogate derivative.

Finite differences that rerun target selection can change the selected position, ranking/membership and height-count scale. They test a different functional dependency from simply holding those fields constant. A mismatch must not automatically be labelled simulator-gradient failure.
The native backward terminal path invokes the selection helper again. Any frozen-target diagnostic must preserve the same explicit target on forward and backward, rather than only freezing forward.
No terminal term was evaluated in this experiment. The original step-999 objective and full horizon remain unverified.
proposed_next_test: Save a separate protocol for an explicitly shortened terminal diagnostic after assessing the development gate.
Record chosen target identity/position, selected-membership hash and scale for base and perturbed runs.
Compare recomputed-target and explicitly frozen-target modes as separate objectives. Preserve native backward semantics and make any diagnostic target override explicit.
Measure loss precision/noise and validate each mode against suitable differences before optimizer or long-horizon claims.

def find_best_particle(self, s, f):
        x = self.sim.get_x()
        used = self.sim.get_used()
        mat = self.particle_mat.to_numpy()
        loss = np.abs(x[:, 1] - 0.05)
        loss[np.logical_not(used)] = 1000
        loss[mat != WATER] = 1000
        best_particle_id = np.argmin(loss)
        self.best_particle_pos.from_numpy(x[best_particle_id])

        dist = np.linalg.norm(x - x[best_particle_id], axis=1)
        dist[np.logical_not(used)] = 1000
        dist[mat != WATER] = 1000
        score = np.argsort(np.argsort(dist))
        self.attraction_score.from_numpy(score)

        x[mat != WATER] = np.array([-100, -100, -100])
        x[np.logical_not(used)] = np.array([-100, -100, -100])
        self.attraction_scale[None] = np.sum(x[:, 1] > 0.55) / 12500
